findings.rule: A referenced note (e.g. heat-treatment 'REF NOTE') must be present on the drawing.
findings.reasoning: The title block specifies heat_treatment as 'REF NOTE', but none of the listed notes (N2 through N8) define a heat treatment specification. The manufacturer has no instruction for hardening or tempering the C-45 steel, which is critical for a cylinder rod mount.
findings.correction: Add a note specifying the required heat treatment (e.g., hardness range, quench and temper parameters) or remove the 'REF NOTE' callout if no heat treatment is required.

findings.rule: Surface treatment must be compatible with the base material.
findings.reasoning: The material is C-45 (medium carbon steel) and the surface treatment is I.Z.B.P. (Trivalent), which is a zinc plating process designed for corrosion protection of steel. Zinc plating does not adhere properly to or protect C-45 in the same manner it does low-carbon steels; typically, C-45 cylinder components require hard chrome plating, black oxide, or phosphate treatments. This pairing suggests a design error or copy-paste from a low-carbon steel drawing.
findings.correction: Verify the intended surface treatment for C-45 material. If corrosion resistance is needed, specify an appropriate finish such as hard chrome plating, phosphating, or black oxide instead of zinc plating.

findings.rule: Internal slot corners must have a radius that a standard end mill can produce without requiring a custom tool.
findings.reasoning: Feature F5 defines a rectangular slot 14 mm wide (D14) by 30 mm high (D15). Feature F6 specifies an R7 fillet at the outer corner of the slot. An R7 internal corner radius requires a 14 mm diameter end mill, which exactly matches the slot width. While technically possible, this leaves zero clearance for tool deflection or step-over, making it difficult and costly to machine cleanly. A slightly smaller radius (e.g., R5 or R6) would allow a standard 10 mm or 12 mm end mill to clear the corner easily.
findings.correction: Reduce the internal corner radius of the slot (F6/D16) to R5 or R6 to allow machining with a standard end mill smaller than the slot width, improving manufacturability and reducing cost.
